correctness.rationale: For all d>=2 and t>=0, K_{d,t} is the cube Minkowski-summed with a diagonal segment. A mean-coordinate slice has interval length ell+t over the (d-1)-dimensional projection, and the ordered coordinate gaps with ell have the Dirichlet(1,...,1) simplex law. Its moments give vol=1+dt, transverse covariance (1+(d+2)t)/(12(1+dt)) and diagonal-direction covariance (1+2t+d t^2)/12, in the stated coordinate normalization. These eigenvalues yield the exact determinant profile, derivative and positive curvature at t=1; anisotropy gap is d*t^2*(3+d*t)/(12*(1+d*t)). Correct for t=0 (cube), t=1 and every real t>0; not Euclidean spectral invariance under arbitrary graph-incidence transforms.
risks: The explicit covariance spectrum is only for the chosen cube-plus-diagonal coordinate model; affine transformations preserve isotropic determinant, not eigenvalues.
